newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Nortel bullish on Asia-Pacific growth.
newsitem.headline: Nortel bullish on Asia-Pacific growth.

text.p: Canadian telephone equipment giant Northern Telecom (Nortel) expects the Asia-Pacific region to provide a focus for growth over the next two or three years, company executives said on Wednesday.

James Long, Nortel's executive vice-president in charge of the Asia-Pacific, told reporters the rapid spread of wireless telephony and deregulation of markets would help its revenue in the region keep expanding by over 30 percent to 2000.

"Our business here is growing in excess of 30 percent per year and we're very optimistic that that will continue at least through until the end of the decade," Long said on the sidelines of an Asian industry conference.

Nortel, which makes phone networks, switching devices and other telecoms equipment, had an annual turnover in the Asia-Pacific region of around US$1 billion last year out of total global sales of US$12.8 billion.
"We will move from a company of somewhere over US$1 billion to three and a half to four billion by the end of the year 2000," Long added.
Nortel president designate and chief operating officer John Roth repeated his recent forecast that the company's global turnover could not be expect to maintain its recent high pace of growth.
"In the first quarter of this year, we saw global order growth of some 35 percent and revenue growth of around 30 percent," Roth said. "I would expect to expand in Asia and Europe.".

Long said Nortel was benefitting like most of its competitors from the expansion of the Asian telecoms industry and was gaining particularly from the entry of new players into the regional and national markets as these were liberalised.
It specialises in making and installing complete telecommunications networks for new companies, providing the equipment for an entire network.
"We're very bullsh on the prospects for Asia. The company is just rising with the tide but the tide is rising very rapidly," Long said.
"Nortel's history is really to be the champion of the new carriers," he said.
Wireless telecommunications, such as mobile phones and radio networks, were also providing a lucrative market, he said.
"Wireless has been the largest single area for us -- but that comes from a very low base."
Roth said Nortel's bigest geographic gains in Asia had come from China, Japan and South Asia.
